newsitem.title: INDIA: India's 96/97 debt inflows to offset outflows - RBI.
newsitem.headline: India's 96/97 debt inflows to offset outflows - RBI.

text.p: Inflows through international debt into India in fiscal 1996/97 will more than offset outflows on account of debt repayment, an official of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said.
"The net figure is more important," the official said, referring to worries among economists and bankers about debt service commitments of about $14 billion during the year.
Some economists have said the bunching of external payments in the second half of 1996/97 (April-March) could lead to sharp volatility in the exchange rate of the rupee.
The net inflow during the year will be about $1.0 billion, the official, who did not want to be identified, said.
Other RBI officials at a weekend conference of foreign exchange dealers in the northern city of Jaipur, said debt repayments during the year should not cause concern.

"The outflows under IDBs (India Development Bonds) and FCNR (foreign currency non-resident deposits held by expatriate Indians) together amounting to $5.0 billion will to a large extent be recycled into the system and net outflows on this account are not expected to be very large," an RBI official told the meeting.

"Although FCNRA liabilities have gone out of the reserves to the extent of almost $6.0 billion in the last three years, there has been an overall increase in non-resident deposits, a good portion of which comes into reserves," the official said.

Even if one assumed that there would not be net inflows of foreign institutional investor (FII) investment into India due to the current slump in the stock markets, India's foreign exchange reserves are expected to be maintained, the official said.
The central bank official said the current level of foreign exchange reserves at $18.4 billion at end-September 1996 represented a rise of $1.4 billion over March 1996.

"During this period, repayments to IMF were a little over $600 million, sales under FCNRA amounted to nearly $1.0 billion (redemption of maturing deposits) and there has been a reduction of $1.0 billion in outstanding forward liabilities," the official said.
"In other words, if these outflows had not been there, reserves would have increased by $4.0 billion."
